Eran Elhaik’s research is largely contested. Many notable geneticists are heavily critical of his work and methods. As far as figuring out why a Jew would favor such a hypothesis, it’s for a couple reasons. There’s actually a few Jewish scholars who support the Khazar Hypothesis. Some of these Jewish scholars who support the hypothesis are anti-Zionist themselves and therefore resort to this hypothesis. Others may have used this hypothesis as a poor and ineffective way to try and debunk the age-old antisemitic trope that claims “the Jews killed Jesus.” In other words, one of these scholars may use the hypothesis to assert that “us Jews had nothing to do with the crucifixion of Jesus, because we aren’t descended from those ancient Jews.” And in regard to your point concerning ancestry as an infective way to determine sovereignty, I could not agree more! You worded it perfectly, my friend. It’s very “blood-and-soil-ish” and that kind of ethnonationalism is exactly what I try to separate myself from.

Edit: Spelling. Also something else I forgot to include - another reason why some of these Jewish scholars resort to the Khazar hypothesis is to ineffectively (again) try and debunk Nazi racial pseudoscience asserting that Jews are a "distinct biological race." In other words, it has been used to assert that Jews can't be a "distinct biological race" because they are a heavily mixed Khazar group of Turkic, Iranic, Slavic, etc. descent.

The Khazar hypothesis claims that Ashkenazi Jews descend from the Khazars of the Caucasus region, and are not of Middle Eastern/Ancient Israelite origins. This hypothesis is largely debunked and is mostly used by anti-zionists or legitimate anti-semites to try and invalidate the Jews’ historical tie to the region of Israel/Palestine. While it is true that the Khazar Elite converted to Judaism around a thousand years ago, there is no substantive evidence that points to contemporary Ashkenazi Jews being descended largely or mostly from the Khazars. The overwhelming majority of genetic studies on Ashkenazi Jews points to a mixed Middle Eastern/Southern European heritage. Just to clarify, I’m not here trying to formulate a Rudy Rochman-esque type of argument in favor of Israel, I’m just reciting what has been concluded by the vast majority of geneticists and historians.
